text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum: free elections in Bosnia are the best confirmation of the success of the Dayton agreement.
- French ambassador to Belgrade Gabriel Keller says delay of local elections in Bosnia will not influence the lifting of sanctions against Yugoslavia as planned 10 days after the elections.
- Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Slobodan Radulovic says there will be no devaluation.
- Gas for Italy's Puglia province would be cheaper if it is channeled from Russia via Yugoslavia and the Adriatic to Brindisi than via central Europe and northern Italy, says Italian official.

- Director of mixed Yugoslav-Russian company Progresgas Trading Toplica Nedeljkovic says a barter gas deal with Russia is the best way to place domestic goods on that market and promote the country's industrial production.
- President of the Kragujevac Zastava group Srboljub Vasovic says government is fulfilling commitments towards Zastava undertaken 1-1/2 months earlier and effects are already visible.
- Management of Zastava car manufacturer says protest of a group of workers of this factory was damaging to the production process and negatively received by its business partners.
- Protest of Kragujevac Zastava arms enters fifth week. Today workers of Zastava car manufacturer to join them.

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says after visit to the U.S. that changes in the country will be felt only after Yugoslavia rejoins international organisations and not as soon as "outer wall of sanctions" is formally lifted.
- Trial of Democratic Party (DS) President Zoran Djindjic continues today. Djindjic is being tried for libel of the Serbian Prime Minister.
- Belgrade confectionary factory Soko Stark exports to stand at $12 million this year, says director Vojislav Djordjevic.
